open_gaps: A defensible "solid-state market share" CANNOT be computed today — not approximately, not with caveats. There is no numerator: QuantumScape has US$0 revenue and has never disclosed a GWh or a cell count; Solid Power's entire revenue line is SK On collaboration money plus DOE grants and went negative in Q2 2026; ProLogium publishes only a cumulative cell count that is a stale floor from H1 2025 and mixes car-audio, consumer and specialty cells; CATL discloses nothing and expects only small-batch production in 2027. And there is no denominator: nothing in this evidence set sizes a solid-state market in either GWh or dollars — SNE's 725.2 GWh / 316.2 GWh is all-chemistry xEV battery usage and cannot be split. The units are also incommensurable across the pool (cells vs GWh vs USD). Any share percentage published today would be manufactured.

No research house in this payload sizes the solid-state segment at all. There is no analogue here to the LightCounting/Cignal/Dell'Oro coverage that exists for optical — no free release giving solid-state market size, growth, or vendor ranking. That absence, not a missing number, is the structural gap.

ProLogium's true cumulative shipments as of 2026-09-16 are unknown. Only the >2.4 million floor, last actually measured at H1 2025, is public — and the company has been ramping a Giga-level facility since early 2024, so the real figure is materially higher by an undisclosed amount.

ProLogium Taoyuan line capacity (~0.5 GWh/yr, quoted as ≈6,000–6,250 80kWh packs) is media-attributed only — carnewschina 2026-09-06, TheNextWeb 2026-09-08, getcarnews 2026-09-09 — and appears nowhere in the company release. No URL for any of those outlets was captured in the payload, so it is deliberately omitted from the entries rather than cited to a link we do not have.

ProLogium's Dunkirk plant staging is irreconcilable across outlets: one account gives 0.8 GWh in 2028 → 4 GWh by 2030 → 12 GWh by 2032, another gives an initial 4 GWh with a 44 GWh maximum design; TheNextWeb explicitly flags the two as not reconcilable. Do not publish a single Dunkirk number as settled.

No cash/runway or disclosure data for SES AI, Ilika or Microvast (MVST) reached this agent. The payload was truncated mid-sentence inside the Solid Power verifier verdict, so those three companies — explicitly requested — have zero evidence here and no pool verdict can honestly be issued for them.
No semi-solid shipment data of any kind is in the payload (WeLion, Ganfeng, Farasis, NIO 150 kWh pack, etc.). The semi-solid leg of the page is entirely unsourced.

No built or funded solid-state manufacturing capacity figure was verified for anyone. QS's 85 GWh is a PowerCo licence ceiling, CATL discloses no GWh, ProLogium's line capacity is media-only. The capacity column of this page currently has no citable content.

The two researchers gave conflicting QuantumScape FY2026 capex guidance — US$40–60m in one record versus ~US$27–37m in the other — and neither verifier addressed the conflict. Do not publish a QS capex figure until it is re-pulled from the shareholder letter or 10-Q.
Solid Power's 2026 equity offering net proceeds of US$121.3m come from researcher notes only; the verifier's text was truncated before that item was confirmed. Re-verify before publishing.

SNE Research does not give per-company shares for CALB, Gotion, EVE, SVOLT or REPT in its free release text — only GWh and YoY. The widely circulated percentages for those five originate from CnEVPost reading SNE's chart image and are not verifiable in the SNE body.

CATL's primary record (深交所互动易) has no citable deep link: every deep-link format returns an empty JavaScript shell. The primary can be named and dated but not linked; only the aggregator copy is clickable.

The rejected-items list was not visible in the payload received, so this sheet cannot report what failed adversarial verification or why — anything a researcher submitted and a verifier killed is invisible to this pass.

The payload delivered was dominated by optical-track entries (roughly 20 of 27 confirmed items concerned optical transceivers/components). Those are excluded from this solid-state sheet by design, but it means the solid-state track was researched far more thinly than the optical one and should not be treated as an equally complete sweep.
citability_verdict: Four source types are safe to cite on a public page, in descending order of strength. (1) SEC filings on EDGAR — QuantumScape's and Solid Power's 10-Qs are primary, permanent, signed under liability, and are the only documents here where anything is legally attested; cite the Archives permalink (or the lighter filing-index URL) and take the filing date from the in-document signature block, never from a search snippet. (2) First-party company releases on the company's own newsroom or its paid wire (ProLogium via prologium.com / GlobeNewswire) — citable and date-confirmable from the in-body dateline, but you must check whether the number is a fresh measurement or recycled boilerplate: ProLogium's ">2.4 million cells" was first announced in July 2025 and merely restated unchanged fourteen months later. (3) Free press releases from a named research house where the number sits in the free body, not behind the report paywall (SNE Research) — citable with the house name plus the exact release date, preferring SNE's English-edition URL; the underlying Monthly Tracker is sold, but the headline table is not. (4) Chinese trade aggregators (OFweek) as a readable secondary only — attribute the primary event (CATL's SZSE 互动易 answer of 2026-09-09) and use the aggregator as the clickable link, because 互动易 is a JavaScript single-page app with no working deep link; take the date from the page's own byline block, since Chinese pages' search-engine dates are unreliable. Not safe to cite: paywalled bodies (Caixin's Davos report — headline and lede only were readable); capacity numbers that appear in media but not in the company release (ProLogium's 0.5 GWh/yr Taoyuan line, the Dunkirk staging); per-company shares read off a chart image by a re-reporter (CnEVPost's figures for CALB, Gotion, EVE, SVOLT, REPT); non-GAAP "customer billings" presented as revenue; and any licence ceiling (QS/PowerCo's 85 GWh) presented as capacity.
